1201: Love is sweeter than strong drink. Drink makes you happy only while you drink it, but love gives great joy that never runs out, even when you only remember it.
1202: Love is sweet in every way. When you think of the one you love, no pain of being apart comes to you.
1203: I felt a sneeze coming, which people say means someone far away is thinking of you, but it faded. Did he start to think of me and then stop?
1204: He lives in my heart all the time. Oh, do I have a place in his heart too?
1205: He keeps me out of his own heart. Is he not ashamed to keep coming into mine again and again, without a break?
1206: I stay alive only by remembering the happy days I spent with him. What else could I live by?
1207: I have never forgotten him, and even remembering him burns my heart. What would happen to me if I ever forgot him?
1208: However much I think of him, he never gets angry with me for it. Isn't that the great kindness my loved one shows me?
1209: My dear life is slipping away as I keep thinking how unkind he is now, the one who used to say, "We two are not separate."
1210: Long live you, Moon! Please do not set, so my eyes can find him, the one who went away but never left my heart.
1211: A dream came to me carrying a message from my faraway love. What special meal can I give that dream, like a guest, to thank it?
1212: If my fish-shaped eyes would only fall asleep when I beg them, I could tell my love, when he comes in my dream, how hard it has been to stay alive.
1213: He is not kind to me while I am awake. But I see him in my dreams, and that is what keeps me alive.
1214: Love's joy comes to me in my dreams, because the dream goes looking for the one who is not kind to me when I am awake, and brings him to me.
1215: Seeing him while I was awake was sweet only while it lasted. Seeing him in a dream is just the same, sweet for the moment I see him.
1216: If there were no such thing as being awake, my love, who comes to me in dreams, would never leave me.
1217: He is cruel and not kind to me when I am awake. So why does he come into my dreams only to hurt me?
1218: When I sleep, he rests on my shoulders. The moment I wake up, he quickly slips back into my heart.
1219: Only women who never see their loved ones in dreams will complain about men who are not kind to them while they are awake.
1220: The people of this town say he left me in waking life. Do they not see him coming to me in my dreams?
1221: Long live you, evening! But you are not a gentle evening. You are a killing time that eats up the lives of wives whose husbands are away.
1222: Bless you, confused evening! Your eyes look dim and sad like mine. Is your partner as hard-hearted as my husband?
1223: The pale evening comes, wet with drops of dew, and makes me feel tired of living. My sorrow keeps on growing.
1224: When my love is not here, evening comes at me like enemies marching onto a killing field.
1225: What good did I ever do for the morning, that it is gentle with me? And what wrong did I do to the evening, that it hurts me so much?
1226: While my husband had not yet left my side, I never knew how much pain evening could bring.
1227: This love-sickness starts as a tiny bud in the morning, grows bigger all day, and bursts into full flower in the evening.
1228: Evening burns like fire, and the cowherd's flute is its messenger. Even that flute has become a weapon that kills me.
1229: When evening spreads over everything and confuses my mind, the whole town seems confused too, and suffers in sorrow just like me.
1230: I think of him, whose mind is set on earning money. In this confusing evening, my life, which has lasted until now, is dying away.
1231: Thinking of him who went far away and left you this sorrow, your eyes have cried away their beauty. Now they feel ashamed in front of the sweet-smelling flowers they once outshone.
1232: My eyes have turned pale and keep filling with tears. They seem to tell everyone that the one I love is no longer kind to me.
1233: On our wedding day my shoulders were full and happy. Now they have grown thin, and they seem to tell everyone loudly that we are apart.
1234: With your partner gone, your gold bangles slip off, and your shoulders have lost their old beauty and fullness.
1235: My thin shoulders, their old beauty gone and their bangles slipping off, tell everyone how cruel the hard-hearted one was to me.
1236: Because my bangles slip and my shoulders are thin, people call him cruel. Hearing him blamed hurts me more than my own pain.
1237: My heart, why not go to that hard-hearted man and tell him how loudly my thin shoulders cry out? Wouldn't that bring you praise?
1238: Once, when I only loosened my arms from our hug, the forehead of my innocent wife with her gold bangles turned pale at once.
1239: When even a little breeze slipped in between us as we hugged, the big, cool eyes of my innocent wife turned pale.
1240: Her bright forehead turned pale first. Did the paleness in her eyes see this and become even sadder?
1241: My heart, won't you think hard and tell me some medicine, any medicine at all, that can cure this sickness of sorrow that nothing else can cure?
1242: Long live you, my heart! He has no love for us, so your suffering over him is just foolish.
1243: My heart, why stay here thinking of him and suffering? The one who gave us this sickness of sorrow has no kind thoughts for us.
1244: My heart, when you go to him, take my eyes with you too. They want so badly to see him that they are eating me alive.
1245: My heart, he does not come to us even when we long for him. But can we really give him up, saying, "He hates us"?
1246: My heart, when you see the one you love, who ends our quarrels with a hug, you cannot even stay upset. So the anger you show him now is fake.
1247: My good heart, either let go of your love or let go of your shyness. I cannot carry both of them at once.
1248: My foolish heart, you are sad that he will not feel sorry for us and be kind. Yet you still run after the one who left us.
1249: My heart, the one we love lives right here inside you. So when you think of him, where are you going to look for him?
1250: If we keep in our heart the one who left us and does not come near, we will lose even more of the beauty we have left.
1251: My self-control was like a door locked tight with the bolt of shyness. But the axe of love smashes that door down.
1252: This thing called love has no pity. Even at midnight, it keeps giving orders to my heart.
1253: I try to hide my love, but it gives no warning. Like a sneeze, it just bursts out.
1254: I used to say I had strong self-control. But my love has come out of hiding and now shows itself for everyone to see.
1255: People sick with love do not know the self-respect that refuses to run after someone who has turned away from them.
1256: How strange is this sorrow that has taken hold of me! It makes me want to follow the very one who turned away from me.
1257: When the one I love, out of love, does the things I long for, I no longer know anything called shyness.
1258: My love is a clever thief with many tricks. Aren't his soft, sweet words the army that breaks down my firmness as a woman?
1259: I went to him meaning to sulk and hold back. But when I saw my heart already rushing to join him, I hugged him.
1260: Can those whose hearts melt like fat thrown into a fire ever say, "We will be close to him and still keep up our sulking"?
1261: My eyes have lost their shine from watching the road for him. My fingers are worn out from touching the marks I made to count the days since he left.
1262: My friend in shining jewels, if I forgot him even now, my arms would lose their beauty and my bangles would slip off.
1263: He went away to win success, with only his own courage for company. I am still alive only because I long to see him come back.
1264: Thinking of the return of the one who left, with all the love we shared, my heart climbs from branch to branch to look out for him.
1265: Let me just see my husband until my eyes are full. Once I have seen him, the paleness on my soft arms will go away by itself.
1266: Let my husband come back, even for one day. I will drink in his love until all this sickness of sorrow is gone.
1267: When he comes back, he who is as dear to me as my own eyes, should I sulk, or hug him, or do both? I cannot decide.
1268: Let the king fight on and win the war. Then I will join my wife at home, and we will have a feast together this evening.
1269: For those who long for the day their faraway love will come back, one day drags by as slowly as seven days.
1270: If her heart breaks with sorrow and she dies, what good will it be that she gets me back, or has me, or even holds me close?
1271: Even though you try to hide it, your eyes, darkened with eye makeup, will not stay quiet. They have something to tell me.
1272: My innocent love, whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders are smooth like bamboo, has a womanly shyness that is even greater than her beauty.
1273: Just as the thread shows through the clear beads strung on it, something shines through this young woman's beauty.
1274: Just as a sweet smell is hidden inside a flower bud that has not opened, something is hidden inside this innocent girl's small, shy smile.
1275: As she left, my love with the tight bangles gave me a secret sign. That sign holds a medicine that cures my deep sorrow.
1276: He hugs me with so much love and joy. But this hints that he is planning to do the hard thing again, leave me, without caring for me.
1277: My bangles knew before I did that my husband, the lord of the cool seashore, had left me.
1278: My love left only yesterday, yet my body has turned pale as if seven days had passed.
1279: She looked at her bangles, looked at her soft shoulders, and looked at her feet. That is what she did there.
1280: People say that to show the pain of love with your eyes, and so to plead with the one you love, is the most womanly thing a woman can do.
1281: To feel joy just by thinking of someone, and to be happy just by seeing them: strong drink cannot do this, but love can.
1282: When love comes in full, as tall as a palm tree, you should not sulk even as much as a tiny grain of millet.
1283: Even if my husband ignores me and does only what he likes, my eyes cannot rest without seeing him.
1284: My friend, I went to him meaning to sulk. But my heart forgot all that and went straight to making up with him.
1285: Just as the eye cannot see the brush that puts dark eye makeup on it, I cannot see my husband's faults at the moment I see him.
1286: When I see him, I see none of his faults. When I do not see him, I see nothing but his faults.
1287: I am like people who jump into a flood knowing it will sweep them away. What is the use of sulking when I know it will not work?
1288: You thief! Even though it brings me shameful pain, your hug is to me what strong drink is to someone who craves it.
1289: Love is softer than a flower. Only a few people know how to enjoy it at its very best.
1290: She showed she was upset only with her eyes. Then, wanting the hug even more than I did, she melted into my arms.
1291: My heart, you have seen how his heart stays on his side alone. So why do you not stay on my side?
1292: My heart, even after seeing that he does not care for me, you still go to him, thinking he will not be angry.
1293: My heart, is it because "people in trouble have no friends" that you leave me and follow him as you please?
1294: My heart, you will not sulk first and then enjoy making up. So who will ever plan such things with you again?
1295: When he is away, my heart fears it will not have him. When he is here, it fears he will leave. So my heart is never free from pain.
1296: Whenever I sat alone and thought of him, my own heart seemed ready to eat me alive.
1297: My foolish heart has no pride and cannot forget him. Stuck with such a heart, I have even forgotten my shyness.
1298: My heart loves him as much as life itself. It thinks that looking down on him would only shame itself, so it keeps thinking of his good points.
1299: When you are in trouble, who will help you, if even your own heart does not?
1300: When your own heart does not act like your family, it is no surprise that strangers do not either.
1301: Hold back your hug and sulk a little. Then we can watch, for a short while, the pain of love that he goes through.
1302: A little sulking is like the right amount of salt in food. Letting it go on too long is like putting in a little too much salt.
1303: Not hugging and making up with the one who is sulking is like adding fresh pain to someone who is already suffering.
1304: Not making up with the one who is sulking is like cutting the root of a vine that is already drooping.
1305: Even for good men with fine qualities, the real beauty is the loving little anger that rises in the hearts of their wives with flower-like eyes.
1306: Love without its big quarrels and small sulks is like fruit that is either too ripe or still hard and green.
1307: Even in a lovers' sulk there is a kind of pain: the worry, "Will our time together last long enough?"
1308: What use is it to feel sad when there is no loved one who will understand, "They are hurting because of me"?
1309: Water is sweet only when it is in the shade. In the same way, sulking is sweet only with those who truly love you.
1310: He leaves my sulk to dry up without comforting me, yet my heart still says, "Let us be with him." That is nothing but pure desire.
1311: You unfaithful man! All women feast their eyes on your broad chest as if it belongs to everyone. So I will not come near it.
1312: While I sat sulking, he sneezed. He knew I would have to break my silence and wish him a long life.
1313: Even if I wear flowers picked from a tree, she gets angry and says I put them on to show off to some other woman.
1314: When I said, "We love each other more than anyone," she sulked and asked, "More than whom? More than whom?"
1315: When I said, "We will never be apart in this life," her eyes filled with tears, as if I meant we would part in the next life.
1316: When I said, "I thought of you," she asked, "So you had forgotten me?" Then, instead of hugging me, she began to sulk.
1317: When I sneezed, she first wished me a long life. Then she took it back and cried, asking, "Who was thinking of you, that you sneezed?"
1318: So I held back my sneeze. Then she cried and said, "Are you hiding from me that your people are thinking of you?"
1319: Even when I comfort her out of her sulk, she gets angry again and says, "So this is how you sweet-talk other women too!"
1320: Even when I just sit and look at her, thinking of her beauty, she gets angry and asks, "Who are you thinking of as you look at me like that?"
1321: Even when he has done nothing wrong, a little sulking can make him show me even more love.
1322: The small pain that a lovers' sulk brings may make his kindness droop for a while, but it will come back even stronger.
1323: Our hearts are mixed together like water and soil. With such a lover, is there any heaven as sweet as a little sulking?
1324: In a sulk that ends with a hug that will not let go, a weapon appears that breaks down my firm mind.
1325: Even when a man has done nothing wrong, being kept for a while from the soft arms of the woman he loves has a joy of its own.
1326: Digesting food is sweeter than eating it. In the same way, in love, sulking is sweeter than being together.
1327: In a lovers' sulk, the one who loses is the one who wins. This becomes clear when they come together again.
1328: By sulking once more, will we win back the sweetness we felt when we came together, when her forehead grew damp with sweat?
1329: Let her with the shining jewels sulk a little longer. And let the night grow longer too, so I can keep pleading with her.
1330: Sulking is the joy of love, and the joy of sulking is to make up and be held close again.
